correctness.rationale: The unit sphere of a finite-dimensional Hilbert space is totally bounded. A finite \(r\)-cover and the infinite pigeonhole principle produce distinct indices whose unit vectors have distance less than \(2r\). The exact identity \(\operatorname{Re}\langle u,v\rangle=1-\|u-v\|^2/2\) then gives correlations arbitrarily close to \(1\), while Cauchy--Schwarz gives the matching upper bound. The proof covers repeated images, injective infinite images, real and complex fields, and does not infer an infinite statement from finite computation. The nonatomic tight-frame construction is verified by direct integration.

value.rationale: The result changes the interpretation of a published continuous Grassmannian optimization and a stated classification problem: on every infinite index set in finite dimension, the proposed pointwise objective is constant rather than a nontrivial packing invariant. It also gives a broad explicit existence class on finite positive nonatomic spaces and identifies sharp boundaries where nontrivial behavior can return: finite index sets and infinite-dimensional spaces. This is a structural clarification of the defined invariant rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or numerical recomputation.
